source.author: dieworkwear (retold)
source.title: Second-hand buying and style for a larger figure (Mr Porter / Put This On, retold)

note: Paraphrased from a user-supplied summary of Derek Guy's second-hand advice and his Mr Porter column on larger men (also Put This On: 'Practical Advice For The Big Guy', https://putthison.com/?p=36603). Retold, not quoted.

rules.rule: Shop second-hand by measurements, not the size label: measure your best-fitting jacket, coat and trousers flat and compare every listing against them.
rules.why: Vintage and cross-brand sizing is inconsistent; the size tag tells you little.
rules.check: Have your benchmark numbers (shoulders, pit-to-pit, back length, sleeve, waist, rise, thigh, hem) ready; ask the seller for any that are missing.

rules.rule: Reject a jacket or coat whose shoulders, length or chest are wrong; sleeves, waist and trouser hems are the cheap fixes.
rules.why: Shoulders, body length and a too-tight chest are hard or impossible to alter.
rules.check: Shoulders within ~1 cm of your benchmark and chest at least your benchmark; everything else is a tailor job.

rules.rule: Check the seam allowance, especially in the trouser seat seam, before buying something that needs letting out.
rules.why: A stocky figure often needs the seat and waist let out; without spare cloth it cannot be done.
rules.check: Ask for a photo of the inside back seam; look for 2–4 cm of folded-in cloth.

rules.rule: Set saved searches with alerts by brand, size and keywords; good pieces in large sizes sell quickly.
rules.why: Supply in larger sizes is thin and turns over fast.
rules.check: Run the same saved search regularly and act on new items.

rules.rule: Search for 'portly', 'stout', 'big & tall' or small-drop cuts; they are cut with room in the stomach.
rules.why: Standard tailoring assumes a 6–7 inch chest-to-waist drop; a small drop fights it. Brooks Brothers, Polo Ralph Lauren and Samuelsohn historically made portly versions.
rules.check: In the listing, waist width should be close to chest width.

rules.rule: Favour quality brands common second-hand: Brooks Brothers, J.Press, Polo Ralph Lauren, Southwick, Samuelsohn, Canali, Corneliani; higher up Isaia, Belvest, Oxxford.
rules.why: Classic makers resell cheaply, especially on Vinted and local boards where sellers misprice them.
rules.check: Prefer natural wool and canvassed or half-canvassed construction.

rules.rule: Inspect condition: shine on elbows and seat, moth holes, snags, worn lining, underarm stains.
rules.why: These are costly or impossible to fix and reduce the garment's life.
rules.check: Ask for close-ups of elbows, seat, lining and underarms.

rules.rule: When unsure between sizes, buy slightly larger and have it taken in.
rules.why: Taking in is easy; letting out depends on spare cloth that may not exist. Larger men often do better in vintage cuts.
rules.check: The shoulders still have to fit; take in only waist, seat or sleeves.

rules.rule: The jacket must cover the seat.
rules.why: A short jacket squares off a heavy figure.
rules.check: From the side, the hem reaches past the curve of the seat.

rules.rule: Prefer a two-button or 3-roll-2 single-breasted jacket for its deep V.
rules.why: A deep V lengthens the torso line.
rules.check: The lapel roll ends at or below the waist button.

rules.rule: With a small chest-to-waist drop, choose a jacket with a fuller top: wider lapels, fuller sleeves, a body that skims the hips.
rules.why: Advice from a large dresser in Derek's Mr Porter piece: room up top balances the midsection. Reference: Jackie Gleason in The Hustler (1961).
rules.check: No pulling across the upper back or sleeves when you reach forward.

rules.rule: Wear a larger shirt collar (spread, or classic with longer points).
rules.why: A small collar makes a large face and neck look bigger.
rules.check: Collar points and spread should look in scale with your jaw.

rules.rule: Choose dark-to-mid tones (navy, grey, brown) in matte, textured cloth such as flannel and tweed; avoid shiny, thin, clingy fabrics and knits that hug the stomach.
rules.why: Sheen and cling show every contour; matte texture drapes.
rules.check: Hold the fabric to light: no shine; knits should hang, not stretch over the stomach.
